metadata.title: Publish and share your project — Milestis Help
metadata.description: Learn how publishing works in Milestis, what kind of link each project gets, and how to share it confidently.

meta.title: Publish and share your project
meta.description: A clear guide to making your project available for sharing and understanding how access works for Memory Books and Portfolios.

related.getting_started: Create and edit your first project

content.publish_p1: In Milestis, publishing means turning your in-editor project into a shareable interactive presentation that can be opened outside the editor. Once published, your project gets a real shareable address and can be viewed on any device.
content.publish_p2: The exact link and access model depend on the format you chose when the project was created.
content.callout_control: Publishing does not mean losing control. You can still take a project offline later and bring it back again when needed.
content.memory_p1: A <strong_tag>Memory Book</strong_tag> is published as a private share link. The published URL includes a viewing token, so the link itself becomes the key to access.
content.memory_p2: This makes Memory Books feel appropriate for personal stories, gifts, family moments, and emotionally sensitive content. Anyone who receives the full link can open the project, but it is not meant to behave like a public showcase page.
content.portfolio_p1: A <strong_tag>Portfolio</strong_tag> is published as a public address. This is the right format when you want people to view your work, evaluate your style, and share it more openly.
content.portfolio_p2: Before publishing, Milestis asks you to choose a slug. That slug becomes part of the live address people will use to open your site, so it is worth choosing something clean, readable, and close to your name or brand.
content.callout_slug: Slugs are part of the public address. Keep them short, clear, and easy to type or share.
content.cost_intro: Publishing uses credits, and the cost depends on the type of project:
content.cost_memory: <strong_tag>Memory Book</strong_tag> uses a tiered cost based on how many photos are included.
content.cost_outro: Before the final publish step, Milestis analyzes the project and shows the expected cost. This gives you a chance to confirm the result, the final link, and the credit usage before making the project live.
content.unpublish_p1: If you need to take a project offline, you can <strong_tag>unpublish</strong_tag> it. This removes public access while keeping the project data intact.
content.unpublish_p2: Later, you can <strong_tag>republish</strong_tag> the project again. This is useful when you want to hide a project temporarily, revise it, or bring back an archived result without rebuilding everything from the start.
content.sharing_intro: Before sending a link to someone else, make one last check:
content.sharing_li1: Open the live preview and make sure the first screen or cover feels finished.
content.sharing_li2: Double-check project titles, dates, and visible text for small mistakes.
content.sharing_li3: For Memory Books, copy the full link so the recipient gets the access token as part of the URL.
content.sharing_li4: For Portfolio projects, choose a slug you will still be comfortable sharing later in your bio, messages, or client communication.
content.sharing_outro: Good publishing in Milestis is not only about making the project live. It is about making sure the first viewer experiences it exactly the way you intended.
